Performers
Artur Schnabel (piano), London Symphony Orchestra (orchestra), Malcolm Sargent (conductor) Documented

The Archive description, photographed LP sleeve and orchestra discography agree. Bolig and the Schnabel chronology identify a Bechstein piano. The later sleeve uses Sargent’s title Sir; that is not treated as evidence of his title at the 1937 session.

[1] [3] [4] [5]
Work version
Unknown Unknown

The exact performing edition is not identified. Bolig explicitly credits Artur Schnabel with the first-movement cadenza; the consulted public-domain score marks the cadenza slot but does not contain his notes. The Archive description says that an earlier file mix-up with K. 595 has been corrected; the current file attribution follows that corrected record, not the superseded review. No bar-by-bar or aural authentication of the transfer has been made.

[1] [5] [7]
Recorded
1937-01-12 Documented

LSO session 0158 distinguishes K. 467, recorded on 12 January, from K. 459, recorded on 9 and 12 January. The date is independently stated in the Archive description and the side-level discographies.

[1] [4] [5] [6]
Place
Abbey Road Studio 1, London, England Documented

The Archive names Abbey Road Studios; the LSO register, Bolig and Schnabel chronology specify Studio 1. The recording venue is not inferred merely from the orchestra’s name.

[1] [4] [5] [6]
Label
Angel Records — Great Recordings of the Century Documented

This is the documented mono LP used for Bob Varney’s transfer, not the original shellac carrier. The original recording was issued by His Master’s Voice.

[1] [3]
Catalogue
COLH 67 Documented

The photographed sleeve prints COLH 67 and pairs K. 467 under Sargent with K. 595 under Barbirolli. LSO session 0158 dates COLH67 to November 1959 and the original K. 467 issue, HMV DB3099–⁠3102, to November 1937. This movement originally occupied DB3099 and DB3100.

[1] [3] [4]
Matrix, take, sides
Probable original-side lineage: 2EA 4604-1, 2EA 4605-1, 2EA 4606-1 and 2EA 4607-2A; first movement parts 1–⁠4 on HMV DB3099–⁠3100. Inferred, not documented

Those issued matrix/take numbers are explicitly documented by Bolig and the Schnabel chronology. Their survival in this particular Angel LP transfer is inferred, not established by runout inspection or take comparison. The LP’s own matrix/runout and pressing are unknown. No original side-join timestamps are assigned. A targeted DAHR search produced no directly usable session record, so no DAHR matrix entry is claimed.

[5] [6] [1]
Transfer
Bob Varney Documented

The source expressly states ‘Transfer by Bob Varney’; this credit is not inferred from the uploader account.

[1] [2]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The item was added on 19 April 2010, and the current MP3 has a later file timestamp following the documented correction. Neither is an identified analogue-to-digital transfer date.

[2]
Processing
Unknown Unknown

The source identifies a mono LP transfer but gives no cartridge, equalisation, noise-reduction, editing or speed-correction procedure. Internet Archive labels the uploaded file VBR MP3 and original; ‘original’ here means the uploaded file, not an original session master.

[1] [2]
Composition rights
Mozart’s concerto is public domain under the ordinary life-plus-70 term; Schnabel’s own cadenza is also beyond that term. Inferred, not documented

Mozart died in 1791; the consulted score derives from the 1878 Breitkopf edition. Schnabel died in 1951, giving an ordinary life-plus-70 expiry at the end of 2021 for his authorship. This is a territorial term calculation, not clearance of every modern edition or a claim about US cadenza publication history.

[7] [8] [6] [5] [10]
Recording rights
territorial — EU public-domain basis: first published in November 1937 on HMV DB3099–⁠3102. Documented

The LSO discography documents publication before 1963, independently of the 1937 session date. The ordinary EU 50-year sound-recording term had expired before the 2013 extension, which applies to recordings still protected at that date. This package uses that territorial basis only. US public-domain status is not established: this is not a recording first published by 1925. The Archive uploader links http://creativecommons.org/licenses/publicdomain/, but that declaration does not independently establish authority to release the performers’ or producer’s rights worldwide. The linked legal URL below is the term basis, not a Creative Commons grant.

[4] [5] [10] [11] [2]

Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, Piano Concerto No. 21 in C major, K. 467, I. Allegro maestoso. Artur Schnabel, piano; London Symphony Orchestra; Malcolm Sargent. Recorded 12 January 1937, Abbey Road Studio 1, London. Transfer by Bob Varney from Angel COLH 67, via Internet Archive. EU territorial public-domain basis; US status not established. DB3100 part 4 explicitly credits Schnabel’s cadenza. Cross-listing on p. 911 confirms the finale’s final side.. Accessed 2026-10-17.

  9. Hannah Chan-⁠Hartley — Mozart, Hewitt & Beethoven’s Fifth, National Arts Centre — K. 467 note: first performance and concert advertisement; twelve-concerto period; musical accounts of all three movements.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
